column1: # Default integration scenario catalog — machine-readable index.
#   scenario_id  group  package  target  exact_test_name  invariant
# `target` is passed verbatim to cargo after `-p <package>` (for example
# normative description and scripts/test-default-scenarios.sh for the runner.
# Acceptance budget: every row must finish within 60 s warm, and the whole
# catalog within 300 s warm. Long-running tests are not admitted here.

column6: invariant
Create persists its intent, then runs lvcreate without the state lock.
Create samples vgs outside the lock or by a bounded epoch retry.
A capacity sample is retried or refused when the allocation epoch moves.
Failed-create compensation runs lvremove without the state lock.
Delete runs its lvs existence check outside the lock.
Delete runs lvremove without the state lock.
Delete refuses to act when the volume changed during the unlocked check.
Move's lvs observation does not hold the state lock.
Move's pvmove start does not hold the state lock.
Grow's lvextend does not hold the state lock.
Grow samples capacity outside the lock under the epoch protocol.
A failed create save rolls back and converges on restart.
A failed compensating lvremove surfaces the orphan instead of claiming success.
A create whose rename landed is honored, not compensated away.
An unreadable durable file still fails closed and compensates.
A failed compensation clear keeps the intent for recovery.
A retry adopts only a verified LV left by a kill window.
A failed delete keeps its durable authorization and fences new authority.
A stale delete intent is dropped without deleting the volume.
A failed delete completion is finished at startup.
A failed delete-intent save leaves the volume untouched.
Create replay is idempotent and payload-exact.
A consumed attachment id cannot be reattached under a stale generation.
Restart preserves attachment state and never moves the generation.
Attachment replay survives a provider restart.
Attachment replay with a different disk id is a typed conflict.
Attachment replay never fabricates a second attachment.
Generation fences are distinct typed refusals.
Reports advance monotonically without changing the generation.
Attachment replay is identity-exact.
A stale expected generation is refused.
Attach replay is idempotent.
Single-writer attachment admission is preserved.
A delete + same-id recreate never reissues a retired attachment generation.
The v3 N-1 fixture imports legacy ids and upgrades without loss.
The legacy tombstone fixture decodes without loss.
The retired-id filter has no false negatives and is bounded.
A malformed filter is refused typed.
A legacy vector merges into an existing filter without loss.
A noncanonical filter with set bits is not treated as empty.
A future schema version is refused without rewriting the file.
A zero schema version is refused typed.
The v3 N-1 fixture seeds the v4 attachment allocator and upgrades on write.
Compaction bounds the log and expires evicted operations.
The tombstone window is bounded and overflow has the documented answer.
Replay evicts and compacts before serving.
A failed compaction never fails a durable append and is retried.
A persistent compaction failure backs off and recovers after growth.
Compaction evicts to fit one frame instead of failing forever.
A post-snapshot record for a snapshot tombstone is still refused.
A pinned in-flight operation is never evicted.
A pin interleaved with compaction preserves the outcome across reopen.
A redriven outcome after window eviction reopens instead of wedging.
The hard ceiling refuses durable appends and recovers after compaction unblocks.
A cannot-fit in-flight set refuses new intents, drains outcomes and recovers.
Journal retention defaults are bounded and mapped to the runtime.
Retention parses and zero bytes disables only the byte trigger.
Invalid retention bounds and unknown keys are refused.
